correctness.rationale: An exact slant-coordinate/azimuth change-of-variables gives the 2D arcsine integral. A uniform x>=Cr expansion supplies the r² and rim r³ coefficients, and the 1/x term integrates to (1-q²)/(16q³L⁴) times r⁴log(L/r). The x=O(r) apex layer and all Taylor remainders contribute O(r⁴), not hidden log terms. Principal-curvature integration agrees, and finite quadrature plus 200000 direct surface samples checked normalization. Fixed 0<q<1 and fixed L>0 only.
